The line graph gives information about ghe employment of American workers in various sectors
from 1930 go 2010.
Overall, throughout the given period, the industrial, technical, and sales & office sectors emerged
as major employers. In contrast, there was a sharp downward trend in the number of people
working in the agricultural sector, becoming the least chosen one by the end of the timeframe.
Regarding industries that gained in popularity, in 1930, virtually no Americans were engaged in
industrial and technical jobs, and only 10% pursued sales and office occupations. Thereafter,
having remained consistent until 1960, Industrial jobs began attracting more workers, with its
percentages rising gradually a peak of roughly 35% in both 2000 and 2010. Similar upward
trends were also witnessed in technical and sales and office positions, as their participation rates
underwent steady increases overall, to around 30% and 20% respectively in the final year, making
them the second and third most common occupations.
On the other hand, despite being the dominant industry in 1930, with approximately 75% ofthe
labor force employed in farming, fishing and foresting, this sector saw a dramatic decline over
the years, reaching a low of only 5% in 2010. Finally, the percentages of workers in other services
rose slightly from 10% to 15% in the first decade, and then fell toa relatively stable level of around
10% for the rest of the period.
